head: 0f8f40f745314c8c927c8fd7511193d2b659af4d

scope_decision.decision: six registered Operations workflows certified on the native owner route
scope_decision.included: Native policy draft/publish/reject/retire, exception open/acknowledge/start/assign/escalate/prioritize/resolve/approve/close/reopen/reject/cancel, queue read and operations summary.
scope_decision.excluded: None in the registered workflows. Field-owned records use the native Field transport rather than the Operations command.
scope_decision.retained_consumer: The retained TypeScript policy/exception application in packages/server-operations/src/adapters/operations-exceptions.ts is no longer called by the product route. It remains a test/public-export consumer for operations.operations-exceptions.integration.
scope_decision.follow_up: No Operations follow-up is required for the six registered workflows.

native_paths.route: packages/feature-apps/src/routes/api/v1/holdings/[holdingSlug]/operations/route.ts reads through nativeOperationsWorkspace/nativeOperationsDetail and writes through nativeOperationsCommand. The retained draftQueuePolicy/reviewQueuePolicy/openOperationsException/changeOperationsException branch was removed; an unset transport returns 503 NATIVE_OPERATIONS_UNAVAILABLE.
native_paths.field: Records and policies owned by Field Service are routed to the native Field operations transport before the Operations command; this is a native owner path, not a legacy fallback.
native_paths.http: The native Operations HTTP backend resolves the current Account session, Company/branch/department scope, module admission and work-selection CAS, then executes the owner command in one serializable unit.
native_paths.summary: The Operations summary is rendered from the native queue read; no separate summary write exists.

gates.name: operations TS unit suites
gates.result: 88/88 across operations.services.unit (services, task-worker display, work-social API) and operations.native-operations-transport.unit

gates.name: operations.native-operations-transport.unit
gates.result: included in the 88-case TS unit run

browser.result: The Operations page at /holdings/acme/projects-routines/operations?company=acme-co rendered with the native queue: 'Current queue 0 active · 0 awaiting review · 0 escalated · 0 past target', queue policy form, exceptions list and field operational exceptions, with no page errors.
browser.historical: The register retains the earlier native browser lifecycle: POS-sale exception acknowledge v2, start v3, assign v4, escalate v5, resolve v6, independent approve v7, close v8, reopen v9, prioritize v10, resolve v11, reject v12, cancel v13; policy publish v2 and retire v3.
browser.limitation: A new browser command journey was not re-run because the development database currently has no published queue policy or source exception fixture. The native Rust HTTP/commands suites and the historical browser lifecycle cover the command path; the page load above proves the native read route and the fail-closed route change.

legacy.removed: The product Operations route no longer imports or calls draftQueuePolicy, reviewQueuePolicy, openOperationsException or changeOperationsException.
legacy.remaining: The retained TypeScript application remains exported and is exercised by operations.operations-exceptions.integration. It is a test/public-export consumer, not a product fallback.
legacy.field: Field-owned records continue to use the native Field operations transport.

notes: The route change removes the last product fallback identified by the e208578b4 correction for the five partial Operations workflows.
No 6-subagent roster or Common frozen-bundle coordination is present; this bundle follows the user-directed execution without claiming that process evidence.
surfaces_scope: The surfaces apply to the six registered Operations workflows. The retained TypeScript application is a test/public-export consumer outside the product route.
